itinerary.cal: No advance permit reservation needed for this zone — pick up a walk-up wilderness permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Info Center; best conditions are typically late July through September once Terror Creek and the approach gullies have melted out.

days.note: From the Goodell Creek Trailhead (600 ft), follow the old road bed then the Terror Creek climber's path — brushy and easy to lose, with a creek crossing — up to a bench camp around 6,000 ft. Reserve a full day; this approach is a known crux of the trip in its own right.
days.title: Approach to Terror Basin / Stump Hollow
days.objective: Reach the 6,000 ft basin below the Southern Pickets

days.note: Cross the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin (~5,800 ft) and camp near the base of the slabs leading up to the saddle between Terror and Degenhardt. A shorter day than Day 1, used to rest and stage for the climb.
days.title: Move to Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Position camp below the Terror-Degenhardt saddle

days.note: A more moderate day than the north-side routes: slabs lead directly from camp to the saddle between Terror and Degenhardt, then a short, steep 4-pitch ridge/face climbs straight to the top, then descended by the West Ridge gully, with rappels, back into Crescent Creek Basin and camp.
days.title: East Ridge summit push

schedule.label: Ascend slabs to the Terror-Degenhardt saddle
Rope up at the base of the East Ridge
schedule.detail: Short, steep 4-pitch line direct to the summit.

schedule.label: Back at Crescent Creek Basin camp
schedule.detail: A notably shorter, less committing day than the north-side routes.

days.objective: Climb the 4-pitch East Ridge to the summit and return

days.note: Reverse the approach: back over the Barrier, down through Terror Basin, and out the Terror Creek climber's path to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Goodell Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day trip: two approach days to Crescent Creek Basin, then a shorter (~9 hr) summit day on the short, steep 4-pitch East Ridge above camp, and a day out. This is the least-popular of Terror's routes and is usually done as one leg of a larger Southern Pickets enchainment rather than a standalone objective.

approach_variants.name: Goodell Creek and Terror Basin, over the Chopping Block col into Crescent Creek Basin, then slabs and talus on the east side to the Terror-Degenhardt saddle
approach_variants.notes: From the Goodell Creek trailhead off SR-20 near Newhalem, follow the old roadbed and Terror Basin climbers' path, about 4 miles then a steep cairned side trail, to the 5,800 ft Terror Basin camp, then continue over the roughly 6,400 ft Chopping Block col into Crescent Creek Basin.
hazards: A descent by a different route than the one climbed, off a large chockstone in a loose gully
The Chopping Block col and Crescent Creek Basin traverse before any climbing
Loose rock throughout, in a range where that is the defining characteristic
The full Goodell Creek approach with roughly 6,000 ft of gain to camp
approach_variants.baseFinding: The route starts at the saddle between Terror and Degenhardt, and you reach it from the basin by its east side on slabs and talus. That saddle is a gap between two named summits, which is what makes it findable without a view: ground rising on both sides of you, falling away ahead. The discriminator against the peak's other lines, and it is a side-of-the-mountain test: the north face and Stoddard Buttress are reached by going over the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col or through McMillan Cirque and down onto the north side, and they start at a snowpatch at the foot of a 2,000 ft wall. The west ridge tops out at the notch between Terror's true and false summits, marked by a large chockstone. This route starts from the Terror-Degenhardt saddle on the east. If you are on the north side of the mountain, or at a chockstone, you are not here. Arrival at the saddle: from Crescent Creek Basin the ground to it is slabs and talus, taken on the saddle's east side. Four pitches at Grade III-IV 5.6 follow. If you are on sustained harder ground, or on more than a handful of pitches, you are not on the East Ridge. What you do not do on the way down, which is the most useful thing the route records: the standard descent is not a reversal of this ridge. It is the west ridge gully back into Crescent Creek Basin, with multiple rappels off a large chockstone. So the day is a traverse of the peak, up one side and down the other, and the chockstone at the top of the west gully is the feature to identify from the summit.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb begins right off the Terror-Degenhardt saddle with a steep hand/off-width crack (offwidth on the left, a narrower finger seam on the right per some parties) — the recognized crux of the route. At least one party rated this section a stout 5.8, though the standard published rating for the climb is II, 5.6.

Continues directly up the crest of the narrow East Ridge on blocky terrain. Rock quality on this ridge is consistently described as some of the loosest, choss-iest in the Pickets, so test every hold and manage rope drag/rockfall for the second.
The ridge is abandoned here for a rising traverse onto the south face to bypass a steeper step, on more loose rock; low-angle but exposed, with limited natural gear placements.

Wraps back up from the south-face traverse for a final section mixing in easy 5th-class moves before topping out directly on Mount Terror's summit, with its small register and exposed views into McMillan Cirque to the north.
